model_scope.reference: OpenAI publishes its REST API as an OpenAPI 3.1 document, which is what the official SDKs are generated from; all three identifiers appear in it at the pinned revision. That establishes the models exist on this API, which prose documentation alone did not. The Structured Outputs contract these rules encode is separately documented at https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs, which states model support as a version range (the gpt-4o-2024-08-06 snapshot and later) rather than a per-model capability flag; these identifiers fall inside that range. Older snapshots inside the range are deliberately excluded, because several limits encoded here have been revised upward since they shipped.

summary: Strict Structured Outputs subset and limits for the current frontier models on the Responses API, where the schema sits under text.format.
coverage: Applies to the model identifiers named, on the Responses API. The schema rules are the documented Structured Outputs contract, which the provider describes for the feature rather than per model; they are recorded against these identifiers because that is the scope this profile was written for, and no claim is made about other models. The keyword restrictions documented as additional for fine-tuned models are carried separately at info severity, since a rendered request that can be routed to one is subject to them. Each identifier is pinned to OpenAI's published OpenAPI document at an exact revision, so the model list is re-checkable by tools/verify_contract_data.py and provider drift is detectable rather than silent. What the artifact establishes is that these models exist on this API; the Structured Outputs contract itself comes from the guide, which scopes support by version range. A dated probe would be the next step up, and this release ships none.
